lessons.title: Personal and Psychological Importance of Religion
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Religion is an organized system of beliefs and worship whose foundation is the divine message. It teaches a person the principles of living, high moral values and the difference between right and wrong, and gives him peace and contentment. Psychology is the science of the human mind and behaviour. This lesson explains what religion and psychology are, how religious upbringing differs from ordinary upbringing, and how religion and psychology both affect a person's thinking and behaviour.

Important Points

  • Religion is an organized system of beliefs and worship, founded on the divine message.
  • Religion teaches the principles of living, high moral values and the difference between right and wrong.
  • Psychology is the science of the human mind and behaviour; it helps us understand thoughts, feelings, emotions and reactions.
  • The blessing of intellect, understanding and perception has been given to man.
  • Religious upbringing is based on principles and teaches a person to understand the beliefs of others correctly; ordinary upbringing lacks this religious guidance.
  • Religious upbringing broadens a person's thinking and makes him a friend to every human being.
  • Religion and psychology basically affect a person's thinking and behaviour.

Religion and Psychology — The Difference

  • Religion helps with moral principles and rules; psychology helps in understanding feelings and emotions.
  • Religion shows a person the purpose of life and teaches gratitude for the blessings of the True Owner; psychology teaches a person to live according to his conscience and society.
  • Religion gives a person spiritual peace; psychology helps in understanding the problems of life in an orderly way.
  • Religion tells about right and wrong and reward and punishment; psychology creates in a person the awareness of the difference between right and wrong.

mcqs.q: What is religion?
options: An organized system of beliefs and worship
mcqs.why: Religion is an organized system of beliefs and worship whose foundation is the divine message. It teaches the principles of living, high moral values and the difference between right and wrong.

mcqs.q: What is the foundation of the teachings of religions?
mcqs.why: The foundation of the teachings of every religion is the divine message — the message that came from the True Owner for the guidance of human beings.

mcqs.q: Psychology is the scientific study of:
mcqs.why: Psychology is the science of the human mind and behaviour. It helps in understanding a person's thoughts, feelings, emotions and reactions.

mcqs.q: The blessing of intellect, understanding and perception has been given to:
mcqs.why: According to the lesson, the blessing of intellect, understanding and perception has been given to man, not to animals, plants or mountains.

mcqs.q: The organized system of beliefs and worship is called:
mcqs.why: The system of beliefs and worship is called religion. Religion is the organized system of beliefs and worship founded on the divine message.

mcqs.q: Religion and psychology basically have an effect on a person's:
mcqs.why: Religion and psychology affect a person's thinking and behaviour. Both shape how a person thinks and how he acts in daily life.

mcqs.q: Religious upbringing is based on:
mcqs.why: Religious upbringing is based on principles and teaches a person to understand the beliefs of others correctly, whereas ordinary upbringing lacks that religious guidance.

mcqs.q: Religion gives a person:
mcqs.why: Religion gives a person spiritual peace, shows him the purpose of life and teaches gratitude for the blessings of the True Owner.

mcqs.q: Psychology helps a person in understanding:
mcqs.why: Psychology helps in understanding feelings and emotions, and helps in understanding the problems of a person's life in an orderly way.

mcqs.q: Religious upbringing makes a person:
options: A friend to every human being
mcqs.why: Religious upbringing broadens a person's thinking and makes him a friend to every human being, because it teaches him to understand the beliefs of others correctly.

lessons.title: Social and Moral Importance of Religion
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Ethics is the science that tells what is right and what is wrong for an individual or a society. The word "Ethics" comes from the Greek word "Ethos", meaning custom, habit and character. This lesson describes the five types of ethics, the difference between religious and secular ethics, and the great importance of religion in forming the morals of society: religion reduces social evils and teaches love, brotherhood and respect, so religion is not a problem but the solution to problems.

Important Points

  • Religion has an important role in the formation of morals in society.
  • The theory of deontological ethics was presented by the German philosopher Immanuel Kant.
  • The word "secular" was first written by George Jacob Holyoake, the English thinker of secular ethics.
  • Two famous books on secular ethics are Kant's "Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals" and Friedrich Nietzsche's "On the Genealogy of Morals".
  • Religion gives social training, reduces evils like theft, robbery and intoxication, and teaches protection of life, property and honour.
  • Religion teaches charity and forbids hoarding and unlawful profit.

The Five Types of Ethics

TypeMeaning
Virtue EthicsHigh character and honest thinking are necessary for every act.
Consequentialist EthicsThe good or bad result of an act is looked at.
Deontological EthicsEvery act is done under duty and consciousness, and doing justice is necessary.
Religious EthicsHuman action is viewed from the religious point of view and compared with religious teachings and customs.
Secular EthicsActions are judged by human perception, moral conscience, mental ability and reason; connection with a religion is not necessary.

mcqs.q: The English word 'Ethics' is taken from which language?
mcqs.why: Ethics is taken from the Greek word 'Ethos', which means custom, habit, character and the God-given ability of correct use.

mcqs.q: Who presented the theory of deontological ethics?
mcqs.why: The theory of deontological ethics was presented by the German philosopher Immanuel Kant. His view was that the foundation of ethics is natural law and good intention is necessary in every act.

mcqs.q: Who was the first person to write the word 'secular'?
mcqs.why: The word 'secular' was first written by George Jacob Holyoake, who was the English thinker of secular ethics.

mcqs.q: The famous philosopher Kant belonged to which country?
mcqs.why: Immanuel Kant was a German philosopher. He presented the theory of deontological ethics and wrote 'Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals'.

mcqs.q: Whose role is important in the formation of morals in society?
mcqs.why: Religion has an important role in the formation of morals in society. It teaches high moral values, love, brotherhood and respect.

mcqs.q: Which type of ethics looks at the good or bad result of an act?
mcqs.why: In Consequentialist Ethics, the good or bad result of an act is looked at. In Virtue Ethics, by contrast, high character and honest thinking are necessary for every act.

mcqs.q: For secular ethics, which of these is NOT necessary?
mcqs.why: Secular ethics decides about the worth of actions through human perception, moral conscience, mental ability and reason, and for it connection with any religion is not necessary.

mcqs.q: The book 'On the Genealogy of Morals' was written by:
mcqs.why: Friedrich Nietzsche wrote 'On the Genealogy of Morals'. Kant's book on the subject is 'Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals'.

mcqs.q: According to the lesson, religion is not a problem but:
mcqs.why: Religion is not a problem, but the solution to problems, because it reduces social evils and teaches the protection of life, property and honour.

mcqs.q: What does 'Ethos' mean?
mcqs.why: The Greek word 'Ethos' means custom, habit, character and the God-given ability of correct use. The word 'Ethics' is taken from it.

lessons.title: Role of Religion in Solving Crises
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

A crisis is a difficult situation that arises in a country or society, such as shortage of things, rising prices or the spread of an epidemic. A national crisis is limited to one country, while a global crisis, like the coronavirus epidemic, affects the whole world. One major cause of crisis is hoarding — collecting and storing things so that an artificial shortage is created and prices rise. Religion gives guidance for solving crises: patience, tolerance, self-reliance, unity, and stopping evils like hoarding.

Important Points

  • Hoarding means storing things to create an artificial shortage in the market so that prices rise.
  • The teacher explained the meaning of crisis with the example of wheat hoarded by landlords.
  • Causes of crises include natural calamities, artificial shortage, hoarding, inflation, epidemics and unlawful activities.
  • Modern-age crises include the coronavirus epidemic, the inflation crisis and the economic crisis.
  • When demand increases compared to supply, the prices of things in the market rise.
  • In the story in the lesson, Sain Dhani's wife sent him to buy flour.
  • Religion teaches fear of the True Owner, patriotism, patience, tolerance, self-reliance and unity for solving crises.
  • In religious books, the solution to every crisis and every problem is present, so religious education helps in solving crises.

mcqs.q: One cause of crisis is:
mcqs.why: The artificial shortage created by hoarding is one cause of crisis. Hoarding means storing things so that a shortage is created in the market and prices rise.

mcqs.q: What should the people do for the solution of a crisis?
mcqs.why: For the solution of a crisis, common people should act with patience and tolerance, and evils like hoarding should be stopped.

mcqs.q: When the prices of things rise in the market, their:
mcqs.why: When demand increases compared to supply, the prices of things in the market rise. This is why hoarding, which creates artificial shortage, raises prices.

mcqs.q: For which thing did Sain Dhani's wife send him to buy?
mcqs.why: According to the story in the lesson, Sain Dhani's wife had sent him to buy flour.

mcqs.q: What helps in the solution of a crisis?
mcqs.why: Religious education helps in the solution of a crisis, because in religious books the solution to every crisis and every problem is present.

mcqs.q: The coronavirus epidemic was an example of:
mcqs.why: The coronavirus epidemic was a global crisis, which closed businesses all over the world, while a national crisis is limited to one country only.

mcqs.q: The teacher explained the meaning of crisis with the example of:
mcqs.why: The teacher explained crisis with the example of wheat: when landlords hoard wheat, an artificial shortage is created, prices rise and common people fall into difficulty.

mcqs.q: Hoarding means:
options: Storing things to create an artificial shortage
mcqs.why: Hoarding means collecting and storing things so that an artificial shortage is created in the market and prices rise. According to the lesson, hoarding is a major cause of crisis.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a cause of crises?
mcqs.why: The causes of crises are natural calamities, artificial shortage, hoarding, inflation, spread of epidemics and unlawful activities.

mcqs.q: Religion teaches, for solving crises:
mcqs.why: Religion teaches fear of the True Owner, patriotism, patience, tolerance and self-reliance, and creates unity and social consciousness for solving crises.

lessons.title: Concept of Sin and Crime
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Sin is the violation of the commands of the True Owner or of religious rules, while crime is the violation of the current law of the country or state. A major sin is a great sin for which severe punishment is told in religious books, which is repeated again and again and for which no repentance is made. Forgiveness of sin is possible through repentance, but for crime, prescribed punishment and respect of the law are necessary. Man is called the "home of error" because error can occur from every human being.

Important Points

  • Original sin means the disobedience of Hazrat Adam (peace be upon him), who ate the fruit of the forbidden tree and was sent from Paradise to the earth.
  • Not every crime is a sin, but when a crime becomes severe and is repeated again and again, it becomes a sin.
  • If the criminal does not get punishment, respect for law will not remain in society.
  • Corruption or dishonesty is counted in sins, crimes and major sins — all of these.
  • Society can be saved from crimes and sins by following religious education, respecting the law, giving prescribed punishment, repenting from sins and creating awareness.

Sin in Different Religions

  • In Islam, lying, gossiping, greed, lust, backbiting, ingratitude and drinking alcohol are counted as sins.
  • In Christianity, pride, greed, anger, jealousy, laziness and overeating are sins.
  • In Sanatan Dharma, greed, anger, attachment, pride, jealousy, gambling and usurping others' rights are counted as sins.
  • Acts counted as sin in all religions include telling lies, stealing, greed, lust, anger, jealousy, pride, backbiting, ingratitude, drinking alcohol and usurping others' rights.

mcqs.q: What is the name of violating the law?
mcqs.why: Violating the law is called crime. Crime is the violation of the current law of the country or state, whereas sin is the violation of the commands of the True Owner.

mcqs.q: Original sin means:
options: The disobedience of Hazrat Adam (peace be upon him)
mcqs.why: Original sin means the disobedience of Hazrat Adam (peace be upon him): the True Owner had forbidden him from a tree in Paradise, but he ate its fruit, and because of it man was sent to the earth.

mcqs.q: The meaning of major sin is:
options: That act for which severe punishment is prescribed in religion
That evil for which there is no repentance
mcqs.why: A major sin is that great sin which is committed again and again, for which severe punishment is prescribed in religious books, and for which no repentance is made before death.

mcqs.q: Corruption or dishonesty is counted in:
mcqs.why: Corruption is a sin as well as a crime, and being a repeatedly committed great evil, it is also counted among major sins.

mcqs.q: Hazrat Adam (peace be upon him) was sent from Paradise:
mcqs.why: Hazrat Adam (peace be upon him) was sent from Paradise to the earth because of the original sin — eating the fruit of the forbidden tree.

mcqs.q: If the criminal does not get punishment, what will happen in society?
options: Respect for law will not remain
mcqs.why: According to the lesson, getting punishment for crime is necessary, otherwise respect for law will end among people.

mcqs.q: Man is called the 'home of error' because:
options: Error can occur from every human being
mcqs.why: Man is called the 'home of error' because man can commit error; the famous saying means that error or mistake can occur from every human being, and errors also have degrees.

mcqs.q: Sin is the violation of:
options: The commands of the True Owner
mcqs.why: The concept of all religions is that sin is the violation of the commands of the True Owner or of religious rules, while crime is the violation of the law of the state.

mcqs.q: Forgiveness of sin is possible when the sinner:
options: Admits his sin, seeks forgiveness and resolves not to do it again
mcqs.why: If the sinner admits his sin, seeks forgiveness and makes a firm resolve not to do it again, the True Owner can forgive him. For crime, however, mere repentance is not enough.

mcqs.q: Which of these are counted as sins in Christianity?
mcqs.why: In Christianity, acts like pride, greed, anger, jealousy, laziness and overeating are sins, as the lesson describes in the concept of sin in religions.

lessons.title: Jainism (Introduction and Development)
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Jainism has existed since eternity and has been revived from time to time. The founder of its present form is the twenty-fourth and last Tirthankar, Mahavira, who started preaching this religion in 569 BC. "Jain" means "conqueror" — one who has controlled his own self and worldly desires. A Tirthankar is a great saint who, after much austerity, attains complete consciousness and shows people the path of liberation. The basic principle of Jainism is ahimsa (non-violence).

Important Points

  • There are twenty-four Tirthankaras of Jainism; the first ten include Rishabha Natha, Ajita Natha, Sambhava Natha, Abhinandana Natha and Sumati Natha.
  • In the fourth century BC, Jainism greatly progressed; in the twelfth century AD its followers settled in many regions of India.
  • Nowadays the followers of Jain Dharma preach their religion in India, Europe, Africa and America.
  • In Jainism, hurting or killing every living being is the greatest sin.

The Two Sects of Jainism

  • Digambar: those who live in natural dress, that is, they have no particular arrangement of clothes.
  • Shwetambar: those who wear white clothes.
  • The difference between the two sects is only this: one adopts natural dress and the other wears white clothes.

mcqs.q: The meaning of the word 'Jain' is:
mcqs.why: 'Jain' means 'conqueror' or 'victor' — one who has controlled his own self and his worldly desires. Technically, the great preachers of Jain Dharma are called 'Jain'.

mcqs.q: The great preachers of Jainism are called:
mcqs.why: The great preachers of Jainism are called Tirthankars — great saints who, after much austerity, attain complete consciousness and show people the path of liberation.

mcqs.q: The number of Tirthankaras of Jainism is:
mcqs.why: There are twenty-four Tirthankaras of Jainism. The twenty-fourth and last Tirthankar is Mahavira, the founder of the present form of Jainism.

mcqs.q: The basic principle of Jainism is:
mcqs.why: The basic principle of Jainism is ahimsa (non-violence). In Jainism, hurting or killing every living being is the greatest sin.

mcqs.q: In Jainism, the greatest sin is:
options: To hurt or kill every living being
mcqs.why: In Jainism, hurting or killing every living thing is the greatest sin, because ahimsa — not hurting any living being — is its basic principle.

mcqs.q: Mahavira started preaching Jainism in:
mcqs.why: Mahavira, the twenty-fourth and last Tirthankar, started preaching this religion in 569 BC. He was born in 599 BC and attained nirvana in 527 BC.

mcqs.q: 'Digambar' means those who:
mcqs.why: Digambar means those of natural dress — the sect of Jainism which lives in natural dress. The Shwetambar sect, by contrast, wears white clothes.

mcqs.q: The Shwetambar sect is known for:
mcqs.why: Shwetambar means those who wear white clothes. The difference between Digambar and Shwetambar is only that one adopts natural dress and the other wears white clothes.

mcqs.q: Jainism greatly progressed in:
mcqs.why: In the fourth century BC Jainism greatly progressed, and then in the twelfth century AD the followers of Jain Dharma settled in many regions of India.

mcqs.q: A Tirthankar attains, after much austerity:
mcqs.why: A Tirthankar is that great saint who, after much austerity, attains 'complete consciousness' and through preaching takes people out of the illusion of the world towards liberation.

lessons.title: Mahavir
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Mahavira, the twenty-fourth and last Tirthankar of Jainism, was born in 599 BC in the village of Kundagrama in Vaishali district of Bihar, in a royal family. His real name was Vardhamana; his father was Siddhartha and his mother Trishala. He did severe austerities in the jungle for twelve years and gained control over his body and soul. His greatest teaching is ahimsa — not hurting any living being. He attained nirvana in 527 BC at Pawapuri, at the age of 72 years.

Important Points

  • According to Mahavira, a person gets sorrows and sufferings because of his karma.
  • Keeping chastity and controlling worldly desires is called Brahmacharya.
  • According to the principle of aparigraha, property beyond need should not be kept; excess earned wealth should be given away in charity.
  • Mahavira's teachings greatly affected the common life of Jains: they practise ahimsa in every act, speak the truth, do not steal, live a life of chastity and give away wealth beyond need in charity.
  • Among Jains, the practice of keeping fasts is very common.

mcqs.q: Mahavira was born in:
mcqs.why: Mahavira was born in 599 BC in the village of Kundagrama in Vaishali district of Bihar. He started preaching in 569 BC and attained nirvana in 527 BC.

mcqs.q: Mahavira was born in the village of:
mcqs.why: Mahavira was born in the village of Kundagrama in Vaishali district of Bihar, in a royal family — not in a poor family.

mcqs.q: Mahavira's real name was:
mcqs.why: Mahavira's real name was Vardhamana. Siddhartha was his father's name and Trishala was his mother's name.

mcqs.q: Mahavira's father's name was:
mcqs.why: Mahavira's father's name was Siddhartha and his mother's name was Trishala. He was born in a royal family of Kundagrama.

mcqs.q: Mahavira's mother's name was:
mcqs.why: Mahavira's mother's name was Trishala. His father's name was Siddhartha and his own real name was Vardhamana.

mcqs.q: For how many years did Mahavira do austerities in the jungle?
mcqs.why: Mahavira did severe austerities in the jungle for twelve years, bore many sufferings, and gained control over his body and soul.

mcqs.q: Mahavira attained nirvana at:
mcqs.why: Mahavira attained nirvana in 527 BC in the town of Pawapuri in Nalanda district of Bihar, at the age of 72 years.

mcqs.q: Mahavira passed away at the age of:
mcqs.why: Mahavira passed away at the age of 72 years, in 527 BC at Pawapuri. The book does not give the number of months and days.

mcqs.q: According to Mahavira, a person gets sorrows and sufferings because of:
mcqs.why: According to Mahavira, a person gets sorrows and sufferings because of his karma — his own deeds.

mcqs.q: Keeping chastity and controlling worldly desires is called:
mcqs.why: Keeping chastity and controlling worldly desires is called Brahmacharya. Jains live a life of chastity as part of Mahavira's teachings.

mcqs.q: Among Jains, which practice is very common?
mcqs.why: Among Jains, the practice of keeping fasts is very common, along with practising ahimsa, speaking the truth and not stealing.

mcqs.q: Mahavira was born in which kind of family?
mcqs.why: The statement 'Mahavira was born in a poor family' is false: he was born in a royal family of Kundagrama, Vaishali, in 599 BC.

mcqs.q: The meaning of ahimsa is:
options: Not to hurt any living being
mcqs.why: The meaning of ahimsa is not to hurt any living being. It is Mahavira's greatest teaching and the basic principle of Jainism.

mcqs.q: According to aparigraha, a Jain should:
options: Keep a great deal of property
Give away excess earned wealth in charity
mcqs.why: According to aparigraha, property beyond need should not be kept; Jains should give away wealth earned beyond need in charity.

mcqs.q: Mahavira's greatest teaching is:
mcqs.why: Mahavira's greatest teaching is ahimsa — not hurting any living being. According to him, hurting or killing any living being is the greatest sin.

lessons.title: Greatness of the True Owner
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

The True Owner is the Creator and Owner of the whole universe: He is from the beginning and will remain forever, He gives sustenance to every thing according to its need, He is Merciful and Kind, Present and Seeing, One and Only, All-powerful and Wise. Man has been created for the purpose of serving His creation. Every good work should be begun with the name of the True Owner, and thanks for His blessings should be offered by remembering Him, obeying His commands and serving His creation.

Important Points

  • The True Owner nourishes everyone, from the ant to the elephant.
  • In every work begun with the name of the True Owner there is blessing.
  • The benefits of remembering His name are: the heart gets peace, life passes well, a person succeeds in this world and in the hereafter, and the True Owner is pleased.
  • For the True Owner, all human beings are equal; He is Present and Seeing everywhere and is the giver of life to every soul.
  • The surroundings around a person are called the environment.
  • The principles of living, dealing and keeping better relations are called 'values'.
  • The verse 'Awwal Allah Aleem Aala Aalam jo Dhani' is from the poetry of Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai.

Serving Creation — The Teaching of Religions

  • According to Islam, the best among people are those who benefit others.
  • According to Christianity, service to humanity is itself service to the True Owner.
  • According to Hindu Dharma, serving others is itself the essence of religion.
  • According to Buddhism, he who lives for others is indeed a human being; Mahatma Gautam Buddha says that he who lives for himself is an animal.

mcqs.q: The surroundings around a person are called:
mcqs.why: The surroundings around a person are called the environment. The principles of living, dealing and keeping better relations, on the other hand, are called values.

mcqs.q: The principles of living, dealing and keeping better relations are called:
mcqs.why: The name of the principles of living, dealing and keeping better relations is 'values'. These principles guide a person's conduct in society.

mcqs.q: He who lives for others is in reality:
mcqs.why: Mahatma Gautam Buddha says that he who lives for himself is an animal, and he who lives for others is indeed a human being.

mcqs.q: Every good work should be begun:
options: With the name of the True Owner
mcqs.why: Every good work should be begun with the name of the True Owner, because in every work begun with His name there is blessing.

mcqs.q: 'Awwal Allah Aleem Aala Aalam jo Dhani' is a verse of:
mcqs.why: This verse is from the poetry of Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai, the great poet who sang the glory of the True Owner.

mcqs.q: The True Owner provides sustenance to:
options: Every thing according to its need
mcqs.why: The True Owner gives sustenance to every thing according to its need; He nourishes everyone from the ant to the elephant.

mcqs.q: According to Islam, the best among people are those who:
mcqs.why: According to Islam, the best among people are those who benefit others. All religions guide man to serve the creation of the True Owner.

mcqs.q: According to Christianity, service to humanity is:
options: Itself service to the True Owner
mcqs.why: According to Christianity, service to humanity is itself service to the True Owner. Hindu Dharma likewise teaches that serving others is the essence of religion.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an attribute of the True Owner?
mcqs.why: The attributes that show the glory of the True Owner are: He is the Creator of the whole universe, from the beginning and forever, Merciful and Kind, Present and Seeing, One and Only, All-powerful and Wise.

mcqs.q: Thanks for the blessings of the True Owner should be offered by:
options: Remembering Him every moment and obeying His commands
mcqs.why: Thanks should be offered by remembering Him every moment, singing songs of His glory, obeying His commands and serving His creation.

lessons.title: Places of Worship and Methods of Worship of the Main Religions
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

A place of worship is the place where the followers of a religion worship their True Owner. Every religion's place of worship has its own name and structure — mosque, church, temple, pagoda, synagogue and gurdwara — but the purpose of all is to worship the one True Owner. This lesson introduces the places of worship of all the main religions and their methods of worship.

Important Points

  • 'Masjid' means the place of prostration; in a mosque there is a mihrab where the imam stands, and domes and minarets.
  • A church is a rectangular hall with a tall tower or dome, pictures of Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him) and Hazrat Maryam (peace be upon her), and the sign of the cross on top.
  • A temple is a rectangular hall with one or more rooms where idols are kept; Hindus worship there, and followers of Jainism and Buddhism also worship in temples.
  • In the gurdwara, the Guru Granth Sahib is recited, kirtan is sung, and in the end langar is distributed.

Places and Methods of Worship

ReligionPlace of WorshipMethod of Worship
IslamMosquePrayer five times daily, Friday prayer in congregation, taraweeh and itikaf in Ramadan
ChristianityChurchWorship, reading the holy book and singing holy songs; Sunday is the special day
HinduismTempleWorship morning and evening, reading the shastras and singing aarti
BuddhismPagodaWorship and meditation
JudaismSynagogueWorship three times a day
SikhismGurdwaraRecitation of the Guru Granth Sahib and kirtan

mcqs.q: Muslims offer which prayers in day and night?
mcqs.why: Muslims offer five prayers in day and night: Fajr, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha — all of these are offered daily in the mosque.

mcqs.q: The special day of worship of Christianity is:
mcqs.why: The special day of worship of Christians is Sunday, when they worship in the church, read the holy book and sing holy songs.

mcqs.q: The Jews' worship takes place in a day:
mcqs.why: Jews worship three times a day in the synagogue: morning, afternoon and evening.

mcqs.q: The worship of Hindus, Jains and Buddhists takes place in:
mcqs.why: The worship of Hindus, Jains and Buddhists takes place in the temple. A temple is a rectangular hall in which idols are kept.

mcqs.q: In the gurdwara, the holy book recited is:
mcqs.why: In the gurdwara, the Guru Granth Sahib is recited and kirtan is sung, and in the end langar is distributed.

mcqs.q: 'Masjid' means:
mcqs.why: 'Masjid' means the place of prostration. In a mosque people stand in rows behind one imam and do bowing and prostrations.

mcqs.q: In a mosque, the imam stands at the:
mcqs.why: In a mosque there is a mihrab, where the imam stands. A mosque also has domes and minarets and a large hall for the rows of worshippers.

mcqs.q: The sign on top of a church is:
mcqs.why: On top of a church there is the sign of the cross. Inside it there are pictures of the crucified form of Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him) or Hazrat Maryam (peace be upon her).

mcqs.q: In the gurdwara, at the end there is distributed:
mcqs.why: In the gurdwara, the Guru Granth Sahib is recited, kirtan is sung, and in the end langar is distributed among the people.

mcqs.q: The followers of Buddhism worship in the:
mcqs.why: The followers of Buddhism worship in the pagoda and meditate there. The pagoda is the place of worship of Buddhism.

lessons.title: Concept of Piety, Compassion, Sympathy and Truthfulness in Religions
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Piety means doing good deeds for the True Owner, remaining firm on one's belief in good and bad times, keeping thoughts, actions and behaviour pure, controlling desires and respecting others. Compassion (mercy) is kindness to the poor, orphans, the sick and the needy, while sympathy is feeling others' sorrows as one's own and helping them. Sympathy is the foundation of every religion, but sympathy beyond limits causes harm. A clemency appeal is the request to get a convict's punishment forgiven or reduced.

Important Points

  • In Islam, the measure of a person's superiority is his piety.
  • Alexander the Great willed that after his death his hands be kept outside the shroud, so the world may see that he went from the world empty-handed.
  • The principle is: he who does not show mercy to others will also not be shown mercy.
  • The instruction of sympathy in the holy books is not only with human beings but with all creation — animals, birds and plants too.
  • Benefits of sympathy: love, peace and cooperation increase in society, the needy are helped, and a person progresses morally and spiritually.

Mercy and Sympathy — The Difference

  • Mercy (compassion): kindness to the poor, orphans, the sick and the needy.
  • Sympathy: considering others' sorrow as one's own sorrow and helping them.
  • Sympathy beyond limits causes harm, because the one who receives charity beyond limits becomes habitual of it and goes away from hard work.

mcqs.q: Having devotion and respect in every act for the True Owner and fear of disobedience is called:
mcqs.why: Having devotion and respect in every act for the True Owner and fear of disobedience is called piety. Piety also means keeping thoughts, actions and behaviour pure and controlling desires.

mcqs.q: On him who does not show mercy to others:
mcqs.why: The principle is that on him who does not show mercy to others, mercy will also not be shown. Mercy should be shown to all creation.

mcqs.q: Because of doing sympathy beyond limits:
mcqs.why: Doing sympathy beyond limits causes harm, because a person becomes habitual of charity and goes away from hard work, which creates social problems.

mcqs.q: The name of feeling others' sorrows and sufferings is:
mcqs.why: Feeling others' sorrows and sufferings is called sympathy. Sympathy is considering others' sorrow as one's own sorrow and helping them.

mcqs.q: The request to get the death sentence forgiven is called:
mcqs.why: The request to get the death sentence forgiven is called a clemency appeal. Its purpose is to request that a convict's punishment be forgiven or reduced.

mcqs.q: Alexander the Great willed that after his death his hands be kept:
mcqs.why: Alexander willed that his hands be kept outside the shroud, so that the world may see that he went from the world empty-handed, for the world is a guest house.

mcqs.q: In Islam, the measure of a person's superiority is:
mcqs.why: In Islam, the measure of a person's superiority is his piety. All the religions of the world give great importance to piety.

mcqs.q: Mercy (compassion) means kindness to:
options: The poor, orphans, the sick and the needy
mcqs.why: Compassion means that a person has mercy and kindness for others; it is kindness to the poor, orphans, the sick and the needy, whereas sympathy is feeling others' sorrow as one's own.

mcqs.q: According to religions, sympathy is the foundation of:
mcqs.why: The concept of religions is that sympathy is the foundation of every religion, and its instruction is not only with human beings but with all creation — animals, birds and plants too.

mcqs.q: The purpose of a clemency appeal is to request that:
options: A convict's punishment be forgiven or reduced
mcqs.why: The purpose of a clemency appeal is to request that a convict's punishment be forgiven or reduced. It is the right of a punished person, and the governor can accept it.

lessons.title: Accountability and Its Effect on Human Character
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Accountability means answerability of responsibility: a person accepts responsibility for his actions and gives account of them to the higher authority. Self-accountability is the review a person makes of his own day's deeds before sleeping — the recipe of successful people. Accountability creates the feeling of responsibility, ends corruption and helps institutions achieve their targets. According to all religions, every person will give account of his deeds to the True Owner after death.

Important Points

  • The authority of accountability is with the government, the high authorities, and the supervisors and heads.
  • The head of the household can also do accountability; accountability is necessary at every level — home, office and society.
  • In the hereafter, the True Owner Himself will take accountability from every person for his deeds.

Benefits of Accountability

  • The feeling of responsibility is created in a person.
  • A person performs his duty with heart and soul.
  • Correct decisions are taken according to need.
  • Institutions and employees achieve their prescribed targets.
  • Self-confidence is created and corruption ends.
  • Without accountability, a person would become heedless of his responsibility and corruption would increase in society.

mcqs.q: The meaning of accountability is:
mcqs.why: The meaning of accountability is keeping answerability, taking account and keeping the feeling of responsibility — all of these.

mcqs.q: The authority of accountability from officials is with:
mcqs.why: The authority of accountability is with the government, the high authorities, and the supervisors and heads — all of these.

mcqs.q: Because of accountability, a person fulfils the given responsibility:
mcqs.why: Because of accountability, a person fulfils the given responsibility with heart and soul, because he knows he will have to give account of it.

mcqs.q: The recipe of successful people is that before sleeping at night, do your own:
mcqs.why: The recipe of successful people is that before sleeping at night, one's own accountability should be done — reviewing the day's good and bad deeds.

mcqs.q: Self-accountability is done:
mcqs.why: Self-accountability is done by oneself: a person himself reviews his day's deeds, habits and character before sleeping.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a benefit of accountability?
mcqs.why: Benefits of accountability include: the feeling of responsibility is created, duties are done with heart and soul, targets are achieved, self-confidence is created and corruption ends.

mcqs.q: In the hereafter, accountability of every person will be taken by:
mcqs.why: In the hereafter, the True Owner Himself will take accountability from every person for his deeds, as the holy books of all religions teach.

mcqs.q: Can the head of the household do accountability?
mcqs.why: Yes, the head of the household can do accountability. Accountability is necessary at every level — in the home, in the office and in society.

mcqs.q: After death, a person has to give account of his deeds to:
mcqs.why: According to the holy books of all the religions of the world, every person has to give account of the deeds done during his life to the True Owner after death.

mcqs.q: If there were no accountability in society:
mcqs.why: If there were no accountability, a person would become heedless of his responsibility and corruption would increase in society.

lessons.title: Importance of Time and Its Observance from the Religious Point of View
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Astronomy is the science of stars and planets, by which the times of worship, festivals and fasts of every religion are prescribed. The natural ways of knowing time are the rising and setting of the sun, the movement of the moon and the earth's revolution around the sun. In Islam, prayer, fasting and Eid rely on the moon (the Hijri lunar calendar); Christianity uses the Christian calendar and Hinduism the Hindu calendar. Observing punctuality — doing every work at its prescribed time — makes a person successful.

Important Points

  • The earth completes one rotation on its axis in 24 hours, by which day and night occur.
  • The earth completes one revolution around the sun in 365 days, by which the year is completed and seasons change.
  • By the movement of the moon, the month is known.
  • Advance news of weather, lunar eclipse and solar eclipse is known through the study of the movement of stars and planets by the experts of astronomy.
  • In Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism also, the times of worship, fasts and festivals are prescribed in the light of astronomy.
  • The earth is a planet.

mcqs.q: The science of stars and planets is called:
mcqs.why: The science of stars and planets is called astronomy. In it, the movement of the sun, moon, stars and planets is studied.

mcqs.q: By the earth rotating around itself are formed:
mcqs.why: By the earth rotating on its own axis, night and day are formed. The earth completes one rotation on its axis in 24 hours.

mcqs.q: The earth's revolution around the sun is completed in:
mcqs.why: The earth completes one revolution around the sun in 365 days, that is, in one year, that is, in 12 months — all of these say the same period.

mcqs.q: In prayer, fasting and celebrating Eid, reliance is on:
mcqs.why: In prayer, fasting and celebrating Eid, reliance is on the moon, because Islam uses the Hijri (lunar) calendar for these times.

mcqs.q: The earth is a kind of:
mcqs.why: The earth is a kind of planet. It rotates on its axis in 24 hours and revolves around the sun in 365 days.

mcqs.q: The Hijri calendar used in Islam is a:
mcqs.why: The Hijri calendar is the lunar calendar, used for the times of fasting, iftar, prayer, Eid and Hajj of Islam.

mcqs.q: The earth completes one rotation on its axis in:
mcqs.why: The earth completes one rotation on its axis in 24 hours, by which day and night occur, and one revolution around the sun in 365 days.

mcqs.q: Advance news of a lunar or solar eclipse is known through:
options: The study of stars and planets by astronomy experts
mcqs.why: Advance news of weather, lunar or solar eclipse is known through the study and calculation of the movement of stars and planets by the experts of astronomy.

mcqs.q: By the movement of the moon is known:
mcqs.why: By the movement of the moon, the month is known; by the rising and setting of the sun, day and night are known; by the earth's revolution, the year and seasons change.

mcqs.q: By observing punctuality, a person becomes:
mcqs.why: By observing punctuality — doing every work at its prescribed time and not wasting time — a person becomes successful, as the lesson teaches.

lessons.title: Etiquettes
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Etiquettes are the principles, rules, behaviours and moral ways prescribed for creating better relations in society, practised in daily life during conversation, meeting, gatherings, religious places, business and travel. Acting on etiquettes beautifies a person's personality, increases honour and confidence, and ends hatred and enmity from society. The golden rule of social etiquette is: behave with others in the same way as you want others to behave with you.

Important Points

  • Mobile phone etiquette: in the office, meeting or gathering, keep the phone switched off or on silent; do not keep a loud ringtone; for an urgent call, say sorry and speak in a low voice.
  • On seeing someone in difficulty, help him in every way; help the injured in an accident and help people cross the road.
  • Addressing others: listen attentively and with respect, answer with softness, do not cut in the middle of the talk, control anger, and avoid abusive language and backbiting.
  • Conduct: walk with dignity, stand in a queue and wait for your turn, wear clothes according to the occasion, and offer your seat to the elderly, women and the disabled.
  • Etiquettes everyone should know include saying please and thank you, introducing oneself, shaking hands properly, holding the door open for others, observing punctuality and keeping the environment clean.

Etiquettes of Meeting

  • Introduce yourself: tell your full name and give a brief introduction of yourself.
  • Shake hands warmly and properly — neither press with excessive force nor cause pain.
  • Observe punctuality: reach at the appointed time, do not make anyone wait, and in case of delay, inform by phone.

mcqs.q: If a mistake happens, one should say:
mcqs.why: If a mistake happens, one should say sorry. Saying please, thank you and sorry are among the etiquettes everyone should know.

mcqs.q: If a time is fixed to meet someone, it is necessary to:
mcqs.why: If a time is fixed to meet someone, it is necessary to observe punctuality: reach at the appointed time and do not make anyone wait.

mcqs.q: During the other's speaking, it is necessary to:
mcqs.why: During the other's speaking, it is necessary to listen attentively and with respect, and not to cut in the middle of the talk.

mcqs.q: One's environment should be kept:
mcqs.why: One's environment should be kept clean. Taking care of cleanliness everywhere is among the etiquettes everyone should know.

mcqs.q: The golden rule of social etiquette is to behave with others as you:
mcqs.why: The golden rule of social etiquette is that you should behave with others in the same way as you want others to behave with you.

mcqs.q: In an office, meeting or gathering, the mobile phone should be:
options: Switched off or on silent mode
mcqs.why: The etiquette of using a mobile phone is to keep it switched off or on silent mode in the office, meeting or gathering, and to speak in a low voice after saying sorry for an urgent call.

mcqs.q: On seeing someone in difficulty, one should:
mcqs.why: On seeing someone in difficulty, he should be helped in every way; the injured in an accident should be helped, and people should be helped in crossing the road.

mcqs.q: While addressing others, one should NOT:
options: Cut in the middle of the talk
mcqs.why: While addressing others, one should listen with attention and respect, answer with softness and control anger; cutting in the middle of the talk and abusive language or backbiting should be avoided.

mcqs.q: One's seat should be offered to:
options: The elderly, women and the disabled
mcqs.why: A person should offer his seat to the elderly, women and the disabled, stand in a queue and wait for his turn, and keep his conduct dignified.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an etiquette of meeting?
mcqs.why: Etiquettes of meeting include introducing oneself by telling one's full name, shaking hands warmly without causing pain, and observing punctuality.

lessons.title: Etiquettes of Places of Worship
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Religious places are holy places where people go to worship, and they increase peace, brotherhood and respect in society. Every person, majority or minority, has the right to worship according to his belief, and no one should be stopped from coming to a place of worship. Common etiquettes for all places of worship are: switch off the mobile phone, wear appropriate and clean clothes, take off shoes outside, sit silently with manners and respect every religion.

Important Points

  • Mosque: take off shoes, go with ablution, cover the head, do not pass in front of one who is praying and do not dirty the mosque.
  • Temple: take off shoes outside, do not use prasad for personal use, participate in worship silently and do not make noise.
  • Church: remain silent before worship, keep library-like silence, participate in the Sunday 'Holy Communion', give full time to worship and say Amen after prayer.
  • Synagogue: go wearing a kippah (cap), do not eat or drink inside, do not put the holy book on the ground and do not make noise.
  • Buddhist temple: take off shoes, wear appropriate dress, do not touch the idol with feet, bow before the idol and do not make noise.
  • Gurdwara: take off shoes, cover the head with a cloth or turban, remain silent during worship, listen to kirtan with manners and take prasad.
  • For giving something, the right hand should be used.

mcqs.q: Before sitting in any place of worship, it is necessary to:
mcqs.why: Before sitting in any place of worship, it is necessary to switch off the mobile phone, wear appropriate and clean clothes and take off shoes outside.

mcqs.q: For giving something, one should use:
mcqs.why: For giving something, the right hand should be used. This is among the prescribed etiquettes observed at places of worship and in society.

mcqs.q: When sitting in a mosque, along with ablution it is necessary to:
options: Take off shoes and cover the head
mcqs.why: When sitting in a mosque, along with ablution it is necessary to take off shoes and cover the head, and one should not pass in front of a person who is praying.

mcqs.q: If a person of another religion comes to your place of worship, then:
mcqs.why: If a person of another religion comes to your place of worship, do not stop him. No one should be prevented from coming to a place of worship regardless of religion, colour, caste or race.

mcqs.q: For sitting in any place of worship, it is necessary to:
options: Remain silent and wear appropriate dress
mcqs.why: For sitting in any place of worship, it is necessary to remain silent and wear appropriate dress, sit with manners and respect every religion and belief.

mcqs.q: In a synagogue, one should go wearing:
mcqs.why: The etiquettes of a synagogue are: go wearing a kippah (cap), do not eat or drink inside, do not put the holy book on the ground, and do not make noise.

mcqs.q: In a church, after prayer one says:
mcqs.why: In a church, one remains silent before worship, participates in the Sunday 'Holy Communion', does not speak loudly during singing, and says Amen after prayer.

mcqs.q: In a gurdwara, the head should be covered with:
mcqs.why: In the Sikhs' gurdwara: take off shoes, cover the head with a cloth or turban, remain silent during worship, listen to kirtan with manners and take prasad.

mcqs.q: In a temple, prasad should NOT be:
mcqs.why: The etiquettes of a temple include: take off shoes outside, do not use prasad or any other thing for personal use, participate in worship silently and do not make noise.

mcqs.q: Religious places increase in society:
mcqs.why: Religious places increase peace, brotherhood and respect in society, because they are holy places where people of every belief go to worship.

lessons.title: Etiquettes of Office and Bank
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

An office is the place where government or private work is done, and the work of employees in government institutions is to serve the public. Before going to an office, keep extra photocopies of the required papers and the identity card together and check them before leaving home. A bank deposits bills, provides loans, opens accounts, deposits cheques, deposits and withdraws money, sends money online and runs saving schemes. In a rush, one should wait for one's turn, and on completion of work, say words of thanks.

Important Points

  • Online transfer means sending money from one account to another account through the bank via the internet.
  • A special saving account is opened for students in the bank, which creates the habit of saving in them.
  • Method of paying a bill: fill the challan, go to the relevant counter, stand in the queue and wait for your turn, pay the amount and obtain the receipt.
  • Method of opening an account: meet the bank manager, get full information about the saving schemes, gain satisfaction, get a saving account of your choice opened and act on its instructions.
  • Inside a bank: keep the mobile on silent, do not speak loudly, count the received money standing aside there itself, and approach the cashier if it is less or more.

mcqs.q: Among the important works of a bank are:
mcqs.why: Among the important works of a bank are depositing bills, providing loans, and opening accounts and transacting — all of these, along with depositing cheques and sending money online.

mcqs.q: The work of employees working in government institutions is:
options: To keep to their own work
mcqs.why: The work of employees working in government institutions is to serve the public, because an office is the place where the public's government or private work is done.

mcqs.q: If there is a rush in the office and bank, a person should:
mcqs.why: If there is a rush in the office and bank, a person should wait for his turn, standing in the queue patiently.

mcqs.q: On completion of work, to the person in front one should:
mcqs.why: On completion of work, words of thanks should be said to the person in front. This is part of the etiquettes of office and bank.

mcqs.q: The purpose of opening a saving account in a bank is:
mcqs.why: The purpose of opening a saving account in a bank is to save. For students, a special saving account is opened, which creates the habit of saving in them.

mcqs.q: Online transfer means:
options: Sending money from one account to another through the bank via the internet
mcqs.why: Online transfer means sending money from one account to another account through the bank via the internet.

mcqs.q: Before going to any office, one should keep together:
options: Extra photocopies of the required papers and identity card
mcqs.why: Before going to any office, extra photocopies of the required papers, identity card, etc. should be kept together, and checked once again at the time of leaving home.

mcqs.q: After receiving money in a bank, it should be:
mcqs.why: After receiving money in a bank, it should be counted standing aside there itself, and in case of being less or more, the cashier should be approached.

mcqs.q: The first step in the method of paying a bill is:
options: Fill the challan of the bill
mcqs.why: The method of paying a bill is: fill the challan of the utility bill, go to the relevant counter, stand in the queue and wait for your turn, pay the amount, and obtain the receipt.

mcqs.q: Students can get this benefit from a bank:
mcqs.why: A special saving account is opened for students in the bank, by which the habit of saving is created in students, and the saved money proves useful in time of need.

lessons.title: Etiquettes of Bus Stand, Railway Station and Airport
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

In the old era people travelled on foot or riding animals, but the present era is the era of science and technology, with fast conveyances like buses, trains and aeroplanes. The bus stand serves all people, especially those without their own conveyance; railway travel is the oldest, comfortable means; and air travel is the fastest. Each place has its etiquettes: observe punctuality, stand in a queue, book tickets in advance and take care of fellow passengers.

Important Points

  • Bus stand: reach 5–10 minutes before the bus time, stand in a queue to board, offer your seat to an old or disabled person, book long-journey tickets in advance, and check your luggage before getting down.
  • Railway station: a travel ticket is absolutely essential for entering the station; keep luggage under your own seat or above; do not carry strongly smelling food; take care of the bathroom's cleanliness; do not stare at anyone.
  • Airport: advance booking is necessary; pack luggage completely and get information about the number and weight of bags; reach before the prescribed time, get luggage weighed and checked in, answer the staff politely, follow security instructions, keep the phone switched off and go to the prescribed gate on the boarding announcement.
  • For air travel, a ticket, identity card, passport or other travel documents and complete packing of luggage are necessary.
  • Travel luggage should be necessary and brief.

mcqs.q: The present era is called:
options: The era of science and technology
The era of literature and justice
mcqs.why: The present era is called the era of science and technology, in which fast conveyances like motor cars, buses, trains and aeroplanes have come.

mcqs.q: The most comfortable and fastest travel is:
mcqs.why: The most comfortable and fastest travel is by aeroplane. The aeroplane is the fastest travel of the modern era.

mcqs.q: Before going on a journey, the necessary works are:
mcqs.why: Before going on a journey, booking the ticket, preparing luggage and reaching before time — all of these are necessary.

mcqs.q: Luggage for use during travel should be:
mcqs.why: Luggage for use during travel should be necessary and brief, and it should be packed completely before the journey.

mcqs.q: To end waiting in travel, one should:
mcqs.why: To end waiting in travel, one should rest, study and use the mobile — all of these are suitable ways to pass the waiting time.

mcqs.q: One should reach the bus stand before the bus time by:
mcqs.why: Punctuality at the bus stand means reaching 5–10 minutes before the fixed time of the arrival of the bus, then standing in a queue to board.

mcqs.q: For entering a railway station, it is absolutely essential to have:
mcqs.why: Advance contact and booking of the ticket are necessary for railway travel, and having a travel ticket is absolutely essential for entering the station.

mcqs.q: The bus stand is especially beneficial for those people who:
options: Do not have their own conveyance
mcqs.why: The bus stand is beneficial for all people, but especially for those who do not have their own conveyance, because through the bus travel is done from village to city and city to city.

mcqs.q: People prefer railway travel because the train is:
mcqs.why: People prefer railway travel because the train is the oldest means of transport, it is comfortable and convenient, and a person can sit comfortably and enjoy the natural scenes.

mcqs.q: Which documents may be needed for air travel?
options: Identity card, passport or other travel documents
mcqs.why: For air travel, these things are necessary: advance booking of the ticket, identity card, passport or other travel documents, and complete packing of luggage.

lessons.title: Etiquettes of the Market
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

The basic work of a market is transacting. Demand means the buyers' need for a thing, and supply means the quantity of that thing present in the market; prices are determined by the effect of demand and supply. In the old era, trade was done in markets with paper currency, while the modern market includes buying and selling through computer and smart phone, digital currency, social media and online marketing. Without marketing, business does not succeed, as the examples of Amazon and Daraz show.

Important Points

  • The means of business in the present era are computer and smart phone, digital currency, social media, Google, My Business, Facebook, Market Place and website — a person can buy and sell sitting at home.
  • Through social media, one's thing or service is conveyed to the buyers and business grows; social media is the important source of modern marketing.
  • Through marketing, the real needs of customers are understood and the thing is promoted.
  • Amazon and Daraz began their institutions from a small level and became big through marketing.
  • The province of Sindh is famous in the whole world because of its handicraft.
  • In the coming era, digital currency will take the place of paper currency.
  • Through education and skill, a person can understand the market and achieve success by acting on the principles of marketing.

mcqs.q: The province of Sindh is famous in the whole world because of:
mcqs.why: The province of Sindh is famous in the whole world because of its handicraft. Its handmade goods are known everywhere.

mcqs.q: In the coming era, in place of paper currency there will be:
mcqs.why: In the coming era, in place of paper currency there will be digital currency. Digital currency is already among the means of modern business and trade.

mcqs.q: For success in business, the beginning should be made:
mcqs.why: For success in business, the beginning should be made on a new scale, because success in every work begins only with taking the first step.

mcqs.q: The important source of modern marketing is:
mcqs.why: The important source of modern marketing is social media. Through it, one's thing or service is conveyed to the buyers and business grows.

mcqs.q: The basic work of a market is:
mcqs.why: The basic work of a market is transacting — buying and selling, in which prices are determined by the effect of demand and supply.

mcqs.q: Demand means:
options: The quantity of a thing in the market
The buyers' need for a thing
mcqs.why: Demand means the buyers' need for a thing, and supply means the quantity of that thing present in the market. Prices are determined by the effect of demand and supply.

mcqs.q: Prices in the market are determined by:
options: The effect of demand and supply
mcqs.why: In the market, prices are determined by the effect of demand and supply, both in the markets of the old era and in the modern era.

mcqs.q: Without marketing, business:
mcqs.why: Without marketing, business does not succeed: if a businessman does not give information about his products to people, his thing will not reach the market.

mcqs.q: Amazon and Daraz began their institutions:
mcqs.why: The famous business institutions of the world, like Amazon and Daraz, had begun their institutions from a small level and became big through marketing.

mcqs.q: In the markets of the old era, trade was done with:
mcqs.why: In the old era, people gathered in the market, bought after seeing the thing, and trade was done with paper currency; in the coming era digital currency will take its place.

lessons.title: Aristotle
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Aristotle, the famous Greek philosopher, was born around 384 BC in Stagira in northern Greece. His father Nicomachus was a royal physician. He entered the school of Plato in Athens, remained associated with teaching, and was the teacher of Alexander the Great. In 335 BC he established his own school in the Lyceum. According to Ptolemy, he has one thousand works, the most important being 'Nicomachean Ethics' in ten parts. He is considered the founder of logic and biology, and his death took place in Chalcis.

Important Points

  • Aristotle worked in logic, physics, meteorology, astronomy, zoology, politics, literature, poetry, aesthetics, ethics and psychology.
  • He acquired his early education from his father; his mother passed away when he was small, and his father died when he was ten years old.
  • At the age of eighteen he went to Athens, which at that time was the centre of knowledge, art and wisdom.
  • He taught Alexander the Great the art of governance and speech, and the lesson that every person is a servant of the True Owner and has the birthright to live a dignified life.
  • Alexander said: 'If Aristotle remains alive, thousands of Alexanders will be prepared, but thousands of Alexanders together cannot prepare one Aristotle.'

Aristotle's Moral Theory

Every person is a seeker of happiness and peace, and real happiness is that which is obtained by doing good deeds. A person's real comfort is not in physical pleasure, but in happiness obtained through rational reasoning; low emotions can be weakened through struggle and rational reasoning.

mcqs.q: Aristotle's father Nicomachus's profession was:
mcqs.why: Aristotle's father Nicomachus was a royal physician, so his profession was medicine. Aristotle acquired his early education from his father.

mcqs.q: The name of Aristotle's teacher is:
mcqs.why: Aristotle's teacher was Plato. Aristotle entered Plato's school in Athens and remained associated with his teacher's teaching.

mcqs.q: Aristotle's famous book about ethics is:
mcqs.why: Aristotle's famous book about ethics is 'Nicomachean Ethics', which consists of ten parts and is the most important of his works.

mcqs.q: Aristotle is considered the founder of:
mcqs.why: Aristotle is considered the founder of logic and biology. He also worked in physics, meteorology, astronomy, zoology, politics, literature and ethics.

mcqs.q: The place of Aristotle's death is:
mcqs.why: Aristotle's death took place in Chalcis. He was born in Stagira in northern Greece and established his school in the Lyceum at Athens.

mcqs.q: Aristotle was born around:
mcqs.why: Aristotle was born around 384 BC in Stagira in northern Greece. In 335 BC he established his own school in the Lyceum.

mcqs.q: Aristotle established his own school in the Lyceum in:
mcqs.why: Aristotle established his own school in the Lyceum in 335 BC, in which the work of education, teaching and research was done.

mcqs.q: According to Ptolemy, the number of Aristotle's works is:
mcqs.why: According to Ptolemy, Aristotle has one thousand works, including books on logic, physics, meteorology, astronomy, zoology, politics, literature and poetry.

mcqs.q: According to Aristotle's moral theory, real happiness is obtained by:
mcqs.why: Aristotle's moral theory is that real happiness is that which is obtained by doing good deeds; a person's real comfort is not in physical pleasure but in happiness through rational reasoning.

mcqs.q: Aristotle taught Alexander the Great:
options: The art of governance and speech
mcqs.why: Aristotle taught Alexander the Great the art of governance and speech, and the lesson that every person is a servant of the True Owner with the birthright to live a dignified life.

lessons.title: German Philosopher Immanuel Kant
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Immanuel Kant, the famous German philosopher, was born around 22 April 1724 AD in Königsberg, Germany, in a poor family whose forefathers had come from Scotland. Of short stature, simple and shy by nature, he met his educational expenses by labour and became a teacher at Königsberg University. After fifteen years of labour he wrote 'Critique of Pure Reason' in 1781 AD, and around 1786 AD 'Critique of Practical Reason'. His famous theory is the deontological moral theory. He died on 12 February 1804 AD in Königsberg, which nowadays is Kaliningrad, a part of Russia.

Important Points

  • Kant worked in philosophy, physics, library, teaching, authorship, mathematics and education.
  • His books include 'Critique of Pure Reason' (1781 AD), 'Critique of Practical Reason' (around 1786 AD) and 'General Natural History and Theory of the Heavens'.
  • He became famous through the epistemological theory of knowledge.
  • In 'Critique of Practical Reason' he stated that the foundation of religion is ethics, and ethics is everlasting, strong and unchangeable.
  • Kant could never marry because of his shy nature and spent his whole life as a bachelor.
  • The deontological moral theory means performing a work that fully meets the moral standard with regular responsibility, keeping one's intention correct without waiting for the result.

mcqs.q: Immanuel Kant belonged to which family?
mcqs.why: Immanuel Kant belonged to a poor family. He was born around 22 April 1724 AD in Königsberg, Germany, and met his educational expenses by doing labour.

mcqs.q: Kant's family's religious affiliation was:
mcqs.why: Kant's family's religious affiliation was with Christianity. His mother was a strict follower woman of Christianity.

mcqs.q: Kant worked in Königsberg University as:
mcqs.why: Kant worked in Königsberg University as a teacher. He remained associated with the field of education and performed teaching services there.

mcqs.q: Deontological moral theory means:
mcqs.why: Deontological moral theory means deontological ethics: performing a work that meets the moral standard with regular responsibility, keeping one's intention correct without waiting for the result.

mcqs.q: Kant's final resting place is located in:
mcqs.why: Kant's final resting place is located in Russia, because Königsberg, where he died in 1804 AD, nowadays is a part of Russia by the name of Kaliningrad.

mcqs.q: Immanuel Kant was born on:
mcqs.why: Immanuel Kant was born around 22 April 1724 AD in Königsberg, Germany. He died on 12 February 1804 AD in the same city.

mcqs.q: 'Critique of Pure Reason' was written in:
mcqs.why: After fifteen years of labour, Kant wrote 'Critique of Pure Reason' in 1781 AD, describing the importance and role of reason in knowledge.

mcqs.q: Kant died on:
mcqs.why: Kant's death took place on 12 February 1804 AD in Königsberg, Germany, which nowadays is a part of Russia named Kaliningrad.

mcqs.q: Kant's forefathers were originally residents of:
mcqs.why: Kant's forefathers were originally residents of Scotland, from where migrating they came and settled in the Königsberg region of Germany.

mcqs.q: According to Kant, the foundation of religion is:
mcqs.why: In 'Critique of Practical Reason', Kant stated that the foundation of religion is ethics, and that ethics is everlasting, strong and unchangeable.

lessons.title: Imam Ghazali (Rahmatullah Alaih)
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Imam Ghazali, born in Tabaran in the region of Tus in Iran, belonged to a family whose profession was related to yarn. He studied under Sheikh Ahmad Razkani, then in Jurjan under Imam Abu Nasr Ismaili, and then in Nishapur under Imam-ul-Haramain. Nizam-ul-Mulk appointed him supervisor of Madrasa Nizamia, and in 485 AH the Abbasid Caliph Muqtadi Billah sent him as ambassador to Begum Turkhan Khatun. He used to write sixteen pages daily; his 'Ihya Ulum al-Din' has four volumes, and its abridgement 'Kimiya-e-Saadat' was translated into Sindhi by Mirza Qalich Baig and into English by Claud Field. His final resting place is at Haruniya in Tus.

Important Points

  • During his learning period, thieves stole his luggage with his written copies; the leader of the thieves returned them but taunted him that knowledge locked in books is of no use — after that, Imam Ghazali memorised those lessons.
  • His books include the subjects of philosophy, logic, Kalam and Sufism.
  • 'Kimiya-e-Saadat' describes religious worships, human affairs, habits, the things that destroy a person and the qualities that give salvation.
  • In his last age, he stayed in his ancestral region and remained busy in worship and austerity along with writing and compiling.

Imam Ghazali's Moral Theory

According to Imam Ghazali, ethics or character is the name of a firm and established habit, which can be good character or, because of bad habits, bad character. People whose nature is good can be improved through education and training, but improving people of bad nature is very difficult. He divided people into four kinds with regard to moral character: those with no discernment of right and wrong; those who know evils but do not practise good deeds; those who know evils yet consider them correct and follow them; and those born and raised in a bad environment.

mcqs.q: Imam Ghazali was born in:
mcqs.why: Imam Ghazali was born in Tabaran, the region of Tus in Iran. His family's profession was related to yarn (spinning).

mcqs.q: Imam Ghazali's family's profession was:
mcqs.why: Imam Ghazali's family's profession was spinning yarn; the name 'Ghazali' is connected with this family background.

mcqs.q: The book 'The Chemy of Happiness' is the English translation of:
mcqs.why: 'The Chemy of Happiness' is the English translation of 'Kimiya-e-Saadat', translated by Claud Field. Mirza Qalich Baig translated the same book into Sindhi.

mcqs.q: Imam Ghazali's final resting place is located in:
mcqs.why: Imam Ghazali's final resting place is located at a place named Haruniya in Tus. He studied in Nishapur but his grave is at Haruniya.

mcqs.q: Imam Ghazali was appointed supervisor of the educational institution:
mcqs.why: Imam Ghazali was appointed supervisor of Madrasa Nizamia by Nizam-ul-Mulk. This was part of his political and diplomatic role.

mcqs.q: 'Ihya Ulum al-Din' consists of:
mcqs.why: 'Ihya Ulum al-Din' consists of four volumes. Imam Ghazali later abridged the same book by the name of 'Kimiya-e-Saadat'.

mcqs.q: 'Kimiya-e-Saadat' is the abridgement of:
mcqs.why: Imam Ghazali first wrote 'Ihya Ulum al-Din' in four volumes, and after that he abridged the same book and prepared it by the name of 'Kimiya-e-Saadat'.

mcqs.q: 'Kimiya-e-Saadat' was translated into Sindhi by:
mcqs.why: 'Kimiya-e-Saadat' was first written in Arabic and then in Persian; Mirza Qalich Baig translated it into Sindhi, while Claud Field translated it into English.

mcqs.q: Imam Ghazali used to write daily:
mcqs.why: According to an estimate, Imam Ghazali used to write sixteen pages daily; that is why the number of his books is considerable.

mcqs.q: In 485 AH, Caliph Muqtadi Billah sent Imam Ghazali as ambassador to:
mcqs.why: In 485 AH, the Abbasid Caliph Muqtadi Billah made Imam Ghazali his ambassador and sent him to Begum Turkhan Khatun, the queen of the Seljuk country.

lessons.title: Florence Nightingale
lessons.notes_html:
Lesson Summary

Florence Nightingale, the founder of modern nursing, was born on 12 May 1820 AD in the city of Florence in Italy, to William Shore Nightingale and Frances Nightingale. During the Crimean War she went with 38 nurses for the treatment of the war wounded and used to visit their tents at night with a lamp in her hand — that is why she is called the 'Lady with the Lamp'. She began regular nursing education at St. Thomas Nursing School in London, the first secular nursing school of the world, and her book 'Notes on Nursing' was published in 1860 AD. She was awarded the 'Royal Red Cross' in 1883 AD and the 'Order of Merit' in 1907 AD, and passed away on 13 August 1910 AD in Mayfair, London.

Important Points

  • Her parents belonged to a prosperous family and prevented her from adopting nursing because nursing was considered of very low rank in that era.
  • She was educated at home and acquired expertise in German, French and Italian languages as well as arithmetic.
  • Considering marriage proposals an obstacle in her aim, she refused marriage.
  • In 1844 AD she took admission as a nursing student in the Lutheran hospital of Germany; in 1853 AD she was appointed supervisor of the women's hospital on Harley Street, London.

The Environmental Theory

By Florence Nightingale's 'environmental theory' is meant that great importance should be given to a suitable environment during the treatment of the sick: for a patient's recovery, fresh air, clean water, better drainage of water, proper arrangement of the environment, cleanliness of food, and light are essential.

mcqs.q: 'Lady with the Lamp' is the title of:
mcqs.why: 'Lady with the Lamp' is the title of Florence Nightingale, because during the Crimean War she herself used to go to the tents of the wounded at night with a lamp in her hand.

mcqs.q: Florence Nightingale was born in:
mcqs.why: Florence Nightingale was born in the city of Florence in Italy, on 12 May 1820 AD. She passed away in Mayfair, London.

mcqs.q: The Crimean War took place in:
mcqs.why: The Crimean War took place in the region of Crimea, which is in Ukraine. Florence went there with 38 nurses for the treatment of the war wounded.

mcqs.q: During the Crimean War, the number of nurses under Florence was:
mcqs.why: During the Crimean War, there were 38 nurses under Florence, trained by her for the treatment of the war wounded.

mcqs.q: The name of Florence Nightingale's book is:
mcqs.why: The name of Florence Nightingale's book is 'Notes on Nursing', published in 1860 AD. She is considered the founder of modern nursing.

mcqs.q: Florence Nightingale was born on:
mcqs.why: Florence Nightingale was born on 12 May 1820 AD in the city of Florence in Italy. She passed away on 13 August 1910 AD in Mayfair, London.

mcqs.q: Florence was awarded the 'Order of Merit' in:
mcqs.why: Florence was awarded the 'Order of Merit' in 1907 AD by the British government. Earlier, in 1883 AD, she had received the 'Royal Red Cross'.

mcqs.q: Florence was awarded the 'Royal Red Cross' in:
mcqs.why: Florence was awarded the 'Royal Red Cross' in 1883 AD in return for her services, and the 'Order of Merit' in 1907 AD.

mcqs.q: Florence began regular nursing education in:
mcqs.why: Florence began regular nursing education in St. Thomas Nursing School in London, which was the first secular nursing school of the world.

mcqs.q: Florence's environmental theory stresses:
options: A suitable environment during the treatment of the sick
mcqs.why: Her environmental theory means that great importance should be given to a suitable environment during treatment: fresh air, clean water, better drainage, cleanliness of food and light are essential for a patient.
